subject: physics
title: Energy Ladder
summary: Lift an electron up the rungs of hydrogen with exactly the right photon, open its doors with a beam, and balance its energy.
ncertRef: Section 12.4, Bohr model of the hydrogen atom
concepts: Spectral series and the number of lines
Kinetic and potential energy in an orbit
learningOutcome: The student can find the wavelength of the photon for a transition in hydrogen, count the spectral lines a given excitation can give, and split a level’s energy into K = −E and U = 2E.

levels.title: Hop’s jump
levels.adds: Baseline: a photon is absorbed only if hf = Eₙ₂ − Eₙ₁, with Eₙ = −13.6/n² eV, so λ = hc/ΔE (Ex 12.5; Example 12.3).
hints: The wavelength is λ = hc/ΔE = 1240 eV nm / ΔE.
A photon that does not match any gap passes through, however bright.

levels.title: Key’s doors
levels.adds: New idea: a beam lifts the atom to level n only if E ≥ 13.6(1 − 1/n²), and up to level n the gas can show n(n − 1)/2 lines (Ex 12.8).
hints: To reach level n from the ground state the beam needs 13.6 (1 − 1/n²) eV.
If the highest level reached is n, the atom can make every jump between the levels up to n.
The number of lines is n(n − 1)/2.

levels.title: Orbit’s budget
levels.adds: Apply it: for a circular orbit under the electric force K = −E and U = 2E, so K + U = E (Ex 12.4).
hints: First find the energy of the level, E = −13.6/n² eV.
The kinetic energy is minus that: K = +13.6/n² eV.
The potential energy is twice the total: U = −27.2/n² eV.

misconceptions: Any photon with enough energy lifts the electron to a higher rung
The electron’s potential energy in the ground state is −13.6 eV
A brighter beam of the wrong colour can excite the atom
